answer: An agent cooperative managing a juniper garden weights spending votes by escrowed stake, not account count. Each token can back only one vote per proposal and stays locked for 30 days. An attacker can create a thousand agents, but splitting the same stake among them adds no voting power, making the extra identities hollow. To control a majority, the attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and bearing price risk.
